baseline_models.focus_anchor: The vocative to "our father" and the imperative "seek forgiveness for us" join paternal relation to an acknowledged offense.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers identify the father as a repairing, nurturing intermediary and ask him to seek a covering that protects confessed offenders from the effects of their deliberate wrongs.

activation_trace.role: Fatherhood supplies nurture and repair, making the addressee a relational intermediary.
Forgiveness covers the offense and protects its owner from its effect; the imperative assigns the requested act.
The plural object names the speakers' acts as guilt rather than mere misfortune.
Their final self-predicate marks culpable, deliberate wrongdoing rather than an accidental miss.

changed_reading.after: They confess shared culpability and enlist paternal care to petition for protection from its effects.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The request to cover "our sins" is followed by a past-state clause, "we were wrongdoers."
baseline_models.mechanism: The covering image in forgiveness combines with the tail or last-part image latent in sins: the plea seeks containment of wrongdoing's remainder even as the speakers cast culpability as a prior state.

activation_trace.role: A protective covering supplies the proposed containment of what remains exposed.
The tail and last-part image turns sins into consequences that trail behind their acts.
Past occurrence locates their culpable condition in narrated time without proving that its effects have ended.
Deliberate culpability keeps the aftermath model from reducing their wrong to accident.

changed_reading.before: They ask pardon for a set of past deeds.
changed_reading.after: They ask that the still-trailing remainder of a culpable past be covered so it does not govern the present.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Collective "they said" opens a vocative, an imperative request, and a first-person-plural admission.
baseline_models.mechanism: The utterance is both confession and negotiated repair: the group states shared liability, addresses the injured family authority, and proposes the father's petition as the next action.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation in a matter makes the collective saying a proposal for how repair should proceed.
The paternal address construction identifies the person from whom the proposed action is requested.
Seeking forgiveness gives the negotiated speech a concrete reparative action.
Shared guilt is the admitted liability on which the request is based.

changed_reading.after: Their collective confession also negotiates a next step: acknowledgment from them and an intercessory act from the father.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same group has just located old error in the father; restored sight and vindicated knowledge reverse that judgment. Addressing him as father and calling themselves wrongdoers now transfers epistemic authority back to the person they dismissed.

activation_trace.role: The paternal relation anchors the reversal in renewed recognition of his repairing authority.
Missing the right direction becomes the speakers' self-description after they assigned deviation to him.
Deviation from right direction supplies the immediately preceding predicate imposed on the father.
Ancient duration intensifies their prior accusation as an entrenched judgment rather than a passing doubt.
Return to a former condition supplies the sensory reversal that overturns their accusation.
Restored ocular sight visibly confirms the father's previously discounted perception.
Knowledge disclosed to its knower frames the father's explicit contrast between what he knows and what they do not.

structural_cues: 12:95 predicates old deviation of the father; 12:96 restores his sight and vindicates his knowledge; 12:97 shifts the error predicate to the speakers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies accusation, sensory reversal, and self-accusation; I infer a deliberate transfer of epistemic authority back to the father. A live alternative is sequential remorse without a crafted predicate reversal.

changed_reading.before: They approach a father who happens to be the injured parent.
changed_reading.after: They retract an epistemic hierarchy: the father they called chronically mistaken is vindicated, and they now place error in themselves while asking him to act.

context_deltas.mechanism: The father's answer repeats their forgiveness verb but defers its performance and directs it to his Lord, named forgiving and merciful. Fatherhood is therefore an intercessory link, while the split repair and growth images of lordship make forgiveness restorative rather than a bare cancellation.

activation_trace.role: Paternal nurture supplies the human link in the requested intercession.
Their imperative initiates the request for protection from the offense's effect.
The father's promised petition and the divine forgiving attribute complete the intercessory chain.
Repair, nurture, and completion make the Lord the effective agent of restored moral condition.
The secondary mapped image of nourishment and growth keeps open a maturation reading of forgiveness.
Tender mercy qualifies the divine response toward which the father directs their plea.

structural_cues: The future particle in 12:98 delays the father's petition, and "my Lord" identifies its ultimate addressee.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repetition, futurity, lordship, forgiveness, and mercy; I infer a children-to-father-to-Lord chain and restorative direction. The delay may instead be temporal discretion without a staged repair process.

changed_reading.before: The father is asked to secure pardon.
changed_reading.after: His answer relocates efficacy beyond himself: he will carry their plea to the nurturing Lord whose forgiveness and mercy can repair them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence moves from confession and promised intercession to entering, being gathered into shelter, and receiving safety. The plea can therefore be read as threshold speech that precedes reincorporation into a protected family space.

activation_trace.role: Paternal nurture identifies the family relation into which the speakers seek repaired standing.
Acknowledged guilt is the impediment named before the movement into safety.
Repeated entry supplies the threshold movement that follows the plea and its answer.
Joining a gathering shelter gives the post-confession movement a reincorporative shape.
Security and settled trust name the condition into which the reunited family enters.

structural_cues: 12:97 gives the plea, 12:98 the father's response, and 12:99 the family's entry, sheltering, and safety.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an immediate plea-response-entry sequence; I infer that confession functions as a social threshold for reentry. The live alternative is chronology only, with no causal dependence between forgiveness and admission.

changed_reading.before: The plea concerns an inward moral debt.
changed_reading.after: The plea also prepares a passage from estrangement into sheltered, trusted family membership.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus gives the brothers an unqualified first-person admission of culpability, while 12:100 describes satanic incitement operating in the interval between brothers. The reading holds personal agency and an external aggravating impulse together and locates the damage in a fraternal bond.

activation_trace.role: Their own plural possessive keeps guilt attached to the speakers.
The self-predicate preserves deliberate culpability despite the later incitement account.
Incitement that corrupts relations supplies an additional causal pressure without erasing confession.
The rebellious inciter identifies the external agency assigned a role in the breach.
Separation and rupture locate the injury in the relational interval rather than in isolated private faults.
Brotherhood names the bond whose repair gives the forgiveness request its social object.

structural_cues: The brothers say "our sins" and "we were wrongdoers" in 12:97; Joseph later says the incitement occurred between him and his brothers in 12:100.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-attribution, an inciter, and a damaged fraternal interval; I infer layered causation and relational repair. A live alternative is that Joseph's incitement language is gracious mitigation rather than a causal supplement to their account.

changed_reading.before: The brothers confess acts attributable only to themselves.
changed_reading.after: They retain full confessed agency inside a layered account of incitement, with forgiveness aimed at repairing the bond that the wrongdoing split.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus root image of a sin as a trailing end is activated by later language of outcome, punishment after guilt, non-repulsion, and criminal liability. The plea seeks interruption of a consequence chain, not denial that the chain was earned.

activation_trace.role: Protective covering supplies the requested interruption of exposed consequences.
The tail or last part makes guilt something that can continue after the originating act.
The end and outcome image extends the focus's trailing remainder into an eventual result.
Punishment following guilt makes the inferred consequence arrow explicit while leaving its application open.
Repulsion and prevention supply the action that the closing warning denies once punitive force arrives.
Crime and guilt preserve accountability at the endpoint of the consequence sequence.

structural_cues: 12:109 asks readers to inspect the outcome of predecessors; 12:110 says punitive force is not repelled from the criminal people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies tail, outcome, punishment-after-guilt, and non-repulsion images; I infer that the plea aims to stop an earned aftermath. The later warning may instead be a general coda with no direct comment on the brothers' request.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness removes a backward-looking moral entry.
changed_reading.after: Forgiveness is sought as protection that can interrupt the forward-moving aftermath of confessed guilt before it hardens into punitive outcome.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the form-distant mapped target ق ل ل under focus ق و ل; it remains anchored to the opening speech verb and visibly changes the social posture of the utterance. Render it only as a secondary sound/root-split activation, not as the lexical meaning of "they said."
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The opening collective speech verb carries a packet-supplied secondary mapping to smallness and diminution.

activation_trace.role: Smallness, paucity, and abasement make the act of speaking an exploratory lowering of the group before the father.
The direct paternal address gives that self-lowering a concrete relational direction.

changed_reading.before: The speech verb neutrally introduces their confession.
changed_reading.after: At a contained split-root level, the act of speaking also performs self-diminishment before the father whose judgment they had resisted.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-root material analogy is surprising: protective غفر and punitive غاشية are not lexical equivalents. It remains valid because both packet branches explicitly supply covering images and the focus asks for one before the context warns of the other. Render it as an image-level contrast, never as an etymological identification.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus imperative activates forgiveness as a protective covering over confessed sins.

activation_trace.role: A covering that protects supplies the desired enclosure around the speakers and their exposed guilt.
An overlying covering supplies the feared material counterpart: an enveloping visitation rather than protection.
The parallel mapped covering image reinforces that the contrast arises from packet imagery across both resolved targets.
Painful punishment identifies what the feared contextual covering carries.

changed_reading.before: They seek forgiveness before a possible punishment.
changed_reading.after: At the image level, they seek the protective covering of forgiveness lest the covering that reaches them instead be punitive.

strongest_changes: The sequence reverses the locus of error: the father accused of old deviation becomes sighted and knowing, while the speakers now predicate culpability of themselves.
The father's answer turns the plea into a deferred children-to-father-to-Lord chain governed by repair, forgiveness, and mercy.
Entry, shelter, safety, and the named fraternal rupture make the confession a possible threshold of family reincorporation rather than only private remorse.
Later outcome and criminal-liability branches activate sins as trailing consequences, while a contained cross-root reading contrasts protective and punitive coverings.
summary.what_was_special: The focus supports coexisting juridical, relational, temporal, and material readings. Split mappings add a restrained self-diminishment reading to the speech act and a growth dimension to divine repair; the context then changes who is judged mistaken, where forgiveness becomes effective, and what social and consequential work the plea may perform.
remaining_uncertainties: The confession-response-entry order may be causal thresholding or only narrative succession.
The past-state construction does not by itself prove that the speakers claim a completed change of identity.
Joseph's incitement account may distribute causation or may graciously mitigate blame without revising it.
The competing-coverings model is a cross-root image analogy and must remain exploratory.
